questions.prompt: An ACR registry uses RBAC Registry + ABAC Repository Permissions. A workload must pull an image from an allowed repository but has only AcrPull. What should be changed?

options.text: Assign Container Registry Repository Reader with any condition covering the repository.
options.explanation: ABAC-enabled registries use the repository roles rather than legacy AcrPull.

options.text: Keep AcrPull and only refresh the token indefinitely.
options.explanation: A token refresh cannot make an unhonored role grant access.

options.text: Assign only Container Registry Repository Catalog Lister.
options.explanation: Listing repository names is not permission to pull their images.

options.text: Assign only Reader on the registry resource.
options.explanation: Control-plane read does not grant repository image access in ABAC mode.

questions.prompt: A deployment must refer to the exact same container image content after a tag is reassigned. Which identifier should it record?

options.explanation: A digest identifies content rather than a mutable tag label.
latest is a mutable tag and may refer to different content later.
A repository can contain many image versions.
A management container does not identify image content.

questions.prompt: A supported Azure service must pull private ACR images without storing a shared registry password. Which approach fits?

options.text: Use its managed identity with the appropriate image pull role for the registry mode.
options.explanation: Managed identity authentication avoids a shared password and still requires authorization.

options.text: Enable the registry admin account and embed its password in the image.
options.explanation: This stores a shared secret and exposes it in the artifact.

options.text: Assign only a display name to the managed identity without roles.
options.explanation: An identity still requires permission to pull the repository.

options.text: Give the registry a public endpoint and assume images become anonymous.
options.explanation: Network reachability does not provide repository authorization.
